title: A finite module over a Noetherian ring complete along an ideal is complete
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $J\subseteq R$ an ideal such that $R$ is $J$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Let $N$ be a finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Then $N$ is $J$-adically complete: the canonical $R$-linear map $N\to\varprojlim_nN/J^nN$, $x\mapsto(x\bmod J^nN)_n$, into the module of compatible sequences is bijective.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor) (3): N^ = N (x)_R R^, applied with R -> R^ bijective; equivalently Lemma 031B (lemma-when-finite-module-complete-over-complete-ring) with the Krull intersection theorem (Lemma 00IP, lemma-intersect-powers-ideal-module-zero) for J in the Jacobson radical (Lemma 05GI)

proof.text: Write $R^\wedge=\varprojlim_nR/J^n$ and $\iota_R:R\to R^\wedge$, $a\mapsto(a\bmod J^n)_n$. By hypothesis ($R$ is $J$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]) $\iota_R$ is bijective; it is a ring map, hence $R$-linear, and so is its inverse $\iota_R^{-1}$. Base change along the $R$-linear maps $\iota_R$ and $\iota_R^{-1}$ [def-weil-module-base-change] gives $R$-linear maps $\iota_R\otimes\mathrm{id}_N:R\otimes_RN\to R^\wedge\otimes_RN$ and $\iota_R^{-1}\otimes\mathrm{id}_N$ in the other direction, inverse to each other by functoriality of $-\otimes_RN$ ($(\iota_R^{-1}\otimes\mathrm{id})\circ(\iota_R\otimes\mathrm{id})=(\iota_R^{-1}\iota_R)\otimes\mathrm{id}=\mathrm{id}$ and symmetrically). Hence $\beta:N\to R^\wedge\otimes_RN$, $x\mapsto1\otimes x$, the composite of the isomorphism $N\cong R\otimes_RN$, $x\mapsto1\otimes x$, with $\iota_R\otimes\mathrm{id}_N$ (note $\iota_R(1)=1$), is bijective. This is the identification $M=M\otimes_RR=M\otimes_RR^\wedge$ in the proof of Stacks 031B. In Lean, first carry out these steps when the module and ring have the same universe, in the proved private helper finiteModuleCompleteSameUniverse.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 031B (lemma-when-finite-module-complete-over-complete-ring, line 22845): 'the map M = M (x)_R R = M (x)_R R^ -> M^'

proof.text: Let $N^\wedge=\varprojlim_nN/J^nN$ with $\iota_N:N\to N^\wedge$, $x\mapsto(x\bmod J^nN)_n$, and let $c_N:R^\wedge\otimes_RN\to N^\wedge$ be the map $a\otimes x\mapsto a\cdot\iota_N(x)$. Since $R$ is Noetherian and $N$ is a finitely generated $R$-module, $c_N$ is bijective by [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-module-tensor] (2) (Stacks 00MA (3), with $A=R$, $I=J$, $P=N$).

For $x\in N$, $c_N(\beta(x))=c_N(1\otimes x)=1\cdot\iota_N(x)=\iota_N(x)$, so $\iota_N=c_N\circ\beta$ is a composite of two bijections (steps 1 and 2) and is bijective: the canonical map $N\to\varprojlim_nN/J^nN$ is bijective, i.e. $N$ is $J$-adically complete. (In Stacks 031B surjectivity of this map comes from Lemma 0315 and injectivity from $\bigcap_nJ^nN=0$; over a Noetherian $R$ both are contained in the bijectivity of $c_N$, so neither Lemma 0315 nor the Krull intersection theorem with Lemma 05GI is needed.) For a module N in an arbitrary universe, Module.Finite.small makes N small in the universe of R. Apply the same-universe result to Shrink N and transport its canonical completion equivalence along Shrink.linearEquiv and AdicCompletion.congr (restricted to R-scalars). AdicCompletion.map_of identifies this transported equivalence with the canonical map of N, so its bijectivity gives the desired completeness.
